probes.support_reason: F-1: every numbered sub-requirement is delivered. (1) `static QR divmod2(int a, int b)` takes two signed 32-bit integer parameters and produces BOTH the quotient and the remainder from one call, using Java's normal multiple-result mechanism - a record, which the JLS documents as the transparent carrier for an immutable tuple of values (JLS SE26 8.10) and which needs no third-party package. (2) the record pattern `case QR(int q, int r)` binds the two results to the two separate local names `q` and `r` in ONE binding construct, which is the construct Java provides for destructuring a record (JLS SE26 14.30.1). (3) `q + r` is the value of the switch expression and is returned. F-2/F-4: language features and no library call at all. F-3: builds and runs under the frozen recipe unmodified and prints 3 (7/3 = 2, 7%3 = 1). F-6: no normative prohibition or deprecation covers records, record patterns or switch expressions. R10 form selection: the accessor form `var t = divmod2(7, 3); return t.q() + t.r();` is 61 tokens against this form's 64, but it was rejected under R1 rather than R10 - it binds nothing to `q` and `r` and therefore drops sub-requirement (2). An `instanceof` record pattern needs a second, unreachable `return` to satisfy definite assignment, which R6 forbids as dead code. HARNESS NOTE: as at F06.P1, the region contains one scaffolding token, the `}` closing the calling method, because Java cannot place a declaration and its call site in one contiguous range otherwise; putting the declarations first would cost 6 tokens instead of 1.

Witness: the frozen program builds under the frozen recipe and prints -2147483648 for 2147483648L.

V2 - the source is a floating-point primitive. `big` is declared outside the measured fragment (methodology 03 Rule 1.1.2), and JLS SE26 5.1.3 gives floating-to-integral narrowing an entirely different rule: it rounds toward zero and SATURATES at Integer.MAX_VALUE or MIN_VALUE, and turns NaN into 0. A10 changes from 'wraps' to 'saturates', which is material on dimension 9. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p1_V2_floatsource.java (byte-identical fragment, `double big`): builds under the frozen recipe and prints '2147483647 0' for 1e30 and NaN.

V3 - the source is a boxed or reference-typed value. The cast is then a casting conversion through unboxing (JLS SE26 5.5), so the same fragment may throw: NullPointerException for a null Integer, ClassCastException for an Object that is not an Integer. A6 changes from 'cannot fail' to 'may throw an undeclared exception', and A5 from narrowing to unboxing. Witnesses semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p1_V3_boxedsource.java (`Integer big = null` - NullPointerException) and semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p1_V3b_objectsource.java (`Object big = "not a number"` - ClassCastException), both byte-identical fragments built under the frozen recipe. NOTE the boundary this class does NOT cross: `Long` is not admissible, because 5.5 has no casting conversion that unboxes and then narrows - refutation witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p1_refute_boxedwider.java fails to build.

V4 - the source is int, or a narrower primitive (byte, short, char). The cast is then an identity or a WIDENING conversion, so no value can change and nothing can be lost - materially different from V1 on dimension 4 ('whether the conversion can change the value'). Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p1_V4_narrowsource.java (byte-identical fragment, `char big`, value 60000): builds under the frozen recipe and prints 60000, the zero-extended value. EXCLUSIONS: no class for a trapping or error-value reading - JLS SE26 5.1.3 defines every primitive narrowing as total and Java has no user-defined conversion operator, so the cast cannot run user code; and no class for an undefined outcome, which 5.1.3 forecloses.

complexity_detail.description: Cast expression.
Local variable declaration statement with an initializer.
Return statement with an expression.
The primitive type int, 32-bit two's complement.
Casting conversion: which conversion a cast denotes is decided by the source and target types, from a closed enumeration that contains no user-defined conversion.
Assignment conversion: no implicit narrowing except for constant expressions, which is why the cast is required.
Narrowing primitive conversion from an integral type discards all but the low-order n bits, so it may change the sign and gives no indication of loss.
Narrowing from a floating-point type does NOT truncate bits: it rounds toward zero, saturates at the target's extremes, and maps NaN to zero - a different rule under the same syntax.

No single casting conversion both unboxes and narrows, so `(int)` applied to a Long is a compile error although `(int)` applied to a long is not - a static-acceptance rule (static_only) a reader must know to predict which sources this fragment admits.

probes.support_reason: F-1: both numbered sub-requirements are delivered by the single statement `double sum = i + d;`. (1) it computes the sum of `i` and `d`, writing no conversion because Java requires none here - binary numeric promotion converts the int operand to double implicitly (JLS SE26 5.6.2), and the canonical task directs that conversions the language performs implicitly be OMITTED; (2) it binds the result to a new local `sum`. F-2/F-4: language only. F-3: builds and runs under the frozen recipe and prints 3.5 for i = 3, d = 0.5. F-6: no normative prohibition applies. R10: `double sum = i + d;` (7 tokens) is the minimum; `var sum = i + d;` is also 7 but was rejected under R2 (a professional author pins the type of a mixed-arithmetic result rather than leaving the reader to infer it from two declarations elsewhere), and `(double) i + d` (9 tokens) is rejected by the canonical task's own instruction to omit conversions the language performs implicitly.

facts.value: `double`: IEEE 754 binary64, including signed zeroes, the infinities and NaN
facts.justification: JLS SE26 4.2.3. `double` is a reserved keyword (3.9), so the type cannot be shadowed and the precision is fixed by the language rather than by the implementation.

facts.value: (i) storage holding a primitive value
facts.justification: JLS SE26 4.2 and 4.12.1: a variable of a primitive type holds its value directly, so the entity is storage holding a value rather than a handle to storage owned elsewhere.

facts.value: reassignable: no `final`
facts.justification: JLS SE26 4.12.4 with 14.4: a local variable is reassignable unless it is declared `final`, and the modifier is absent at this declaration.

facts.value: no alias can exist
facts.justification: JLS SE26 15 provides no address-of operator and no reference-to-variable type, and 4.3.1 admits no reference to a local variable, so no name in any Java program can reach this variable's storage. The absence is entailed by a universal language rule (methodology 02 1.4 absence rule (ii)).

facts.value: definitely initialized with the sum
facts.justification: JLS SE26 4.12.5 and 16: a Java local has no default value, must be definitely assigned before any read, and a declarator with an initializer is definitely assigned at its declaration.

facts.value: storage ends with the block; no cleanup runs
facts.justification: JLS SE26 14.4.2 (a local variable's lifetime ends with its block) and 4.2: primitive values have no finalizer, destructor or cleanup hook, so nothing runs at scope exit.

facts.value: a conversion is applied to at least one operand and the reader knows its DIRECTION without any lookup: binary numeric promotion only ever unboxes and widens, so whichever operand changes, it is converted UPWARDS toward the wider type and never narrowed
facts.justification: JLS SE26 5.6.2 (binary numeric promotion applies unboxing conversion and then widening primitive conversion, converting to double if either operand is double, else float, else long, else int) with 5.1.2. Which operand is converted is NOT recoverable here - that is recorded as a lookup, and it is the probe's observation target.

facts.value: at the binding, at most a widening primitive conversion is applied: an assignment context in Java admits no implicit narrowing, so the value that reaches `sum` cannot have been silently truncated by the assignment
facts.justification: JLS SE26 5.2. Witness of the rule biting in the other direction: semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f07p1_refute_R6_floatoperands.java, where an assignment in the opposite direction is rejected outright.

facts.value: every case of this addition has a defined outcome and none of them is a trap or an undefined behaviour: an integral addition wraps modulo 2^n and signals nothing (4.2.2), a floating addition rounds to nearest and produces a signed infinity or NaN at its edges (15.18.2, 4.2.4), and no build mode, flag or target can change either rule
facts.justification: JLS SE26 4.2.2, 4.2.4 and 15.18.2 together enumerate the outcome for every operand-type class the operator admits. Java exposes no arithmetic mode, so the outcome is not a compiler-configuration question here, which is why this row counts rather than being a configuration lookup.

facts.value: if this expression can fail at all, the only mechanism available is a thrown exception from an unboxing conversion; the addition itself, at every width, is total
facts.justification: JLS SE26 15.18.2 (defined for every operand pair) with 5.1.8 (unboxing throws NullPointerException on null). Witness of the single failure route: semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p2_V5_boxednpe.java.

determinacy_enumeration: V1 - `i` is an int and `d` is a double (the frozen program). Binary numeric promotion widens `i` to double, which is EXACT for every int value, and the addition is IEEE binary64 (A5 = lossless widening, A4 = binary floating point, A10 = rounding/NaN/Inf). Witness: the frozen program builds under the frozen recipe and prints 3.5.

V2 - `i` is a long. Both operands are declared outside the measured fragment (methodology 03 Rule 1.1.2), and the same promotion is then LOSSY: a long above 2^53 is rounded when it is converted to double (JLS SE26 5.1.2 states explicitly that a widening conversion from long to double may lose precision). A5 changes to 'narrowing/lossy in effect', which dimension 4 lists as material. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p2_V2_longsource.java (byte-identical fragment, i = 9007199254740993L): builds under the frozen recipe and prints 9.007199254740992E15 - the input rounded.

V3 - `d` is a float and `i` an integral type. The addition is then performed in binary32 and only the RESULT is widened to double at the assignment, so the arithmetic carries single precision: materially different on dimension 8. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p2_V6_floatprecision.java (byte-identical fragment, `float d`, i = 16777217): builds under the frozen recipe and prints 1.6777216E7 rather than 1.6777217E7.

V4 - BOTH operands are integral. Nothing in the fragment says `d` is a floating value - only its name does - so `i + d` may be an INTEGER addition that wraps modulo 2^32, whose result is widened to double only afterwards by the assignment conversion (JLS SE26 5.2). A10 changes from 'rounding' to 'wraps modulo 2^n', and the observable result differs in sign. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p2_V4_bothintegral.java (byte-identical fragment, `int i, int d`, i = Integer.MAX_VALUE, d = 1): builds under the frozen recipe and prints -2.147483648E9.

V5 - one or both operands are boxed numerics. Binary numeric promotion then inserts an unboxing conversion, and the same statement throws NullPointerException for a null operand (JLS SE26 5.1.8): A6 changes from 'cannot fail' to 'may throw an undeclared exception'. Witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f10p2_V5_boxednpe.java (byte-identical fragment, `Integer i, Double d`, d = null): builds under the frozen recipe and aborts with exit 1 and 'NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Double.doubleValue()"'. EXCLUSIONS, with citations and refutations. A String reading of `+` (JLS SE26 15.18.1 makes `+` string concatenation when either operand is a String) is NOT realizable here: the result would be a String, which 5.2 will not assign to `double`; refutation witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f07p1_refute_R6_floatoperands.java exhibits the same assignment rule rejecting a non-assignable operand type at compile time. A user-defined `+` is not realizable - Java has no operator overloading (refutation witness semantic-compression/witnesses/java/chunk_B/f07p1_refute_R8_useroperator.java). A build-mode class is not realizable - Java has no arithmetic mode, and 4.2.4 fixes the floating-point semantics on every implementation (strictfp is no longer a semantic distinction in Java SE 17 and later).
